title: Chapter 116 — Onboarding & The 90-Day Ramp
intro: The first week, the curriculum as ramp plan, gates and ramp economics.

sections.title: The Cost of Bad Onboarding
sections.content:
A bad hire costs 3-6 months of productivity and poisons floor culture. But a bad onboarding of a good hire costs almost as much. The new rep who is thrown on the floor in week two without proper training will develop bad habits that take months to fix.

The 90-day ramp is an investment. The first month costs you — the new rep is not producing while they learn. The second month they start contributing. The third month they should be self-sufficient. That investment pays back for years.

sections.title: The Ramp Structure
sections.content:
Week 1-2: shadow the best rep, learn the floor, learn the POS, memorize five key products. Week 3-4: assisted selling with mentor nearby, start one brand family deep dive. Month 2: guided independence with T.O. support, begin Daily Five, complete Zone 1 training. Month 3: full rotation, weekly one-on-ones, 90-day goal measurement.

Every new hire gets a buddy — not the manager, a peer. The buddy handles cultural integration and the 'dumb questions' that new people are embarrassed to ask their boss.

sections.title: Ramp Gates
sections.content:
Set clear milestones. By week 2: pass the floor layout test and POS basics. By week 4: complete the first solo sale. By month 2: achieve minimum close rate on assisted ups. By month 3: hit the 90-day revenue target.

If a new hire is not meeting gates, the coaching conversation happens early — not at 90 days when it is too late. 'You are at 15 percent close rate and the gate is 20 percent. Let me watch your next three ups and we will figure out where the gap is.'
